verdict.rationale: Rive documents an official MCP server that connects the Rive Editor to AI tools. It also documents RML, a text-based XML representation of Rive files that coding agents can create and modify, which gives agents structured access to file content. However, the documented MCP tools are aimed at generating content (View Models, State Machines, Layouts, Shapes) rather than at an agent reading design context to implement a design elsewhere. missing for 10: documented read access to frames, variables, screenshots and component mappings via MCP or API, any public design-context API (no OpenAPI found), and hands-on or independent corroboration of agent design-to-code workflows.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my coding agent can pull real design context — frames, variables, screenshots, component mappings — through an MCP server or API to implement the design

citations.quote: You can connect the Rive Editor to AI tools through MCP (Model Context Protocol).
The first set of tools are designed to let AI handle repetitive tasks, like creating complex View Models, State Machines with hundreds of states/layers, Layouts, Shapes, and more.
RML uses XML to describe the objects and relationships in a Rive file
It lets you create and modify Rive content as code, making it possible to build Rive files with coding agents and other text-based workflows instead of working exclusively in the Editor.
